rules: One hue, four weights — never a rainbow.
Unavailable metrics are disabled with a stated reason, never drawn as a zero line.
Main UI shows compact figures (18.4M); tooltips and tables show exact ones (18,421,842).
Zero and unknown are different: '0' is data, 'Unavailable' is the absence of it.

narrative.overview: Orbit is a workbench, not a website. Every surface is drawn by the GPU through GPUI, so the chrome stays flat, honest, and quiet while the data — transcripts, diffs, graphs, usage — carries the density. There is one accent (ember orange) and it is rationed: selection, focus, the caret, the active series. Everything else is ink on canvas at three weights of emphasis.
keyCharacteristics: One accent, rationed: ember marks the active thing and nothing else.
Hairlines over boxes: a 1px border separates; cards are the exception.
Three ink weights: primary, secondary, tertiary/labels.
Density with air: 28-34px controls, 6-10px padding, 44px page headers.
Ten palettes, one grammar: every color is read from the theme global, never hardcoded.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Ember appears on at most 10% of any screen. If two things are ember, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Ink Weight Rule
rules.body: Emphasis comes from ink weight and size, never from hue. A number that must shout gets a larger size, not a color.

rules.name: The Size-Not-Weight Rule
rules.body: Sizes step 11-12-13-15-20; weights use only 400, 500, 600. No 700+, no tracking tricks below -0.01em.

rules.name: The Tabular Figure Rule
rules.body: Any column of numbers uses fixed-width rendering and is right-aligned; compact forms in the main UI (18.4M), exact forms in tooltips and detail tables (18,421,842).

rules.name: The Border-Or-Shadow Rule
rules.body: A surface declares one: either a 1px hairline or a shadow. Never both, or it reads as a ghost card.

dos: Do read every color, size, and radius from the theme; add a semantic role when a new need appears so all ten palettes stay legible.
Do use hairlines and whitespace to separate sections; reserve bordered surfaces for objects that are conceptually singular (composer, metric board, popover).
Do keep controls at 28px (compact) / 34px (primary) so a 900px-tall window shows 15+ table rows.
Do mark unavailable data in words ('Cost unavailable'): zero and unknown are different facts.
Do pair color with a non-color signal (arrow, icon, label) for any state.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent hue; categorical series use one accent ramp plus neutral inks.
Don't wrap every row in a card, nest a card inside a card, or use a card where a hairline-separated section reads better.
Don't use display fonts, gradients, glass, glow, or emoji in the chrome.
Don't animate decoration; motion is 120-200ms and only confirms a state change.
Don't show a metric the underlying data cannot support — no invented latency, cost, or retry counts.
